reviews.comment: There was only about 1 homework a week. Exams were fair, and we were allowed 1 cheat sheet with anything on it. I never went to lecture, but watching recorded lectures did help a lot. Overall, this was an easy course, and Professor Pantoja was very kind and receptive to questions and concerns. She truly did care about us and the subject matter.

Very kind, but lectures are not very engaging and I could never read her handwriting. She also was often corrected by my peers when working example problems. I found it easier to teach myself during the homeworks. Her class was not my favorite? But she was very sweet.

Took her during a COVID semester, but her lecture delivery was still crap. The way she talked through the slides was hard to follow and her handwriting was unreadable. I learned more from just doing the homework than I did from any of the lectures. If you don't already know all of the subject matter for this class, just look for another professor.

Very caring and intelligent professor who cares dearly about the subject matter and her students. Very easy to talk to one-on-one, easy to access via email and will respond even at 11:30 pm if needed, doesn't expect too much, and allows cheat sheets for the test.

Attendance is not technically mandatory, it is worth 1% of your grade. I only showed up for exams and did well. She's very nice and tests are easy. She allows a full cheat sheet of pretty much anything written on it, front to back, and any calculator. If you struggle with math go to lecture, otherwise you probably don't have to.

hard to follow in a class lecture setting due to her lack of confidence and experience, but when you meet with her one-on-one in office hours she's a lot of help. she's very lenient and offers extra credit to help her student's grades when needed. overall, not a great professor yet (has potential) but is very nice & communicates well
